title: A download that leaves its folder

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo downloads three proofs by name.

tasks.title: Catch a download from outside the proofs folder
tasks.description:
Before you change anything, prove the hole. In `src/reproduce.js`, implement `reproduceProofEscape()`.

Pick a `fileName` that leads out of the proofs folder to a file that exists, and run it through the original `readProof()` with `PROOFS_DIR`. Return an object with:

- `fileName`: the name you used
- `shown`: exactly what `readProof(PROOFS_DIR, fileName)` returned

The check runs your function against the original `proofs.js`. It passes when `shown` is real and is the text of a file outside the proofs folder.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.js` and look at the names it downloads.
Look at the folders beside `proofs` in your workspace.
Write a name that climbs out of `proofs` and into one of them.
Run the demo again and read what `shown` holds.
hints: readProof joins the folder and the name and reads whatever file that gives.
In a path, .. means the folder above. A name that starts with it leaves proofs at once.

tasks.title: Keep every download inside the proofs folder
tasks.description:
Fix `readProof(proofsDir, fileName)` in `src/proofs.js` so it can only ever read files inside `proofsDir`.

- A name that leads to a file inside the folder gives its text, folders in the name included, and dots in a file name are just part of it.
- A name that leads anywhere outside the folder gives `null`: names with `..`, full paths, and folders beside it whose names start the same.
- A name inside the folder with no file gives `null`.

The check downloads honest and unfriendly names from a copy of your workspace whose files outside `proofs` are real.
nextSteps: Work out the full path a name leads to before you read anything.
Work out the full path of the folder the same way.
Compare the two so a folder that merely starts with the same letters does not count.
Run `node src/demo.js` and check the real proofs still download.
hints: The cause is that the name is trusted to stay inside. Looking for .. in the name, or removing it, judges how the name looks, not where it leads.
path.resolve() turns the folder and the name into one full path with every .. followed. Then the question is whether that path is inside the folder.
Resolve the folder and the file, then refuse unless the file's path starts with the folder's path followed by path.sep.

videos.title: How a file name climbs out of its folder

tasks.title: Write the test that would have caught it
tasks.description:
Write vitest tests in `src/proofs.test.js` that guard this hole for good. Call `readProof()` with `PROOFS_DIR` from `folders.js`.

The check runs your test file four times: beside the original `proofs.js` (it must fail), beside a correct fix (it must pass), beside a fix that only checks the full path starts with the folder's path (it must fail) and beside a fix that gives `null` for every name (it must fail).
nextSteps: Ask for a name that climbs out of `proofs` and expect `null`.
Add a name the starts-with fix lets through.
hints: Keep one test that a real proof still downloads, so a fix that refuses everything fails it.
The path of proofs-staff starts with the path of proofs. What does a check on the start of the path make of it?
